modules.title: Software Process, Process Models and Requirements Engineering

topics.title: Software Process Structure
topics.definition: A software process is the set of activities and results needed to build a software product.

children.title: Framework activities
children.definition: Communication, planning, modelling, construction and deployment.

children.title: Umbrella activities
children.definition: Project tracking, risk management, quality assurance, configuration management and reviews that run across the whole project.

children.title: Process framework and task sets
children.definition: A generic framework is tailored by defining task sets, work products and quality checkpoints for the project.

children.title: Process patterns and assessment
children.definition: Reusable solutions to recurring process problems, checked against a capability maturity model such as CMMI.

topics.title: Process Models and Activities
topics.definition: A process model is a strategy for organising the framework activities over the life of a project.

children.title: Waterfall model
children.definition: Sequential phases from requirements to maintenance; simple and document driven but inflexible to change.

children.title: Incremental model
children.definition: Delivers the product in increments, each adding usable functionality, which gives early feedback.

children.title: Prototyping model
children.definition: A throwaway or evolutionary prototype clarifies unclear requirements before full development.

children.title: RAD model
children.definition: Rapid Application Development uses component based construction in short cycles with heavy user involvement.

children.title: Spiral model
children.definition: Risk driven iteration through planning, risk analysis, engineering and evaluation quadrants.

children.title: V model and concurrent model
children.definition: The V model pairs each development phase with its testing phase; the concurrent model shows activities happening in parallel states.

children.title: Specialised and unified process
children.definition: Component based, formal methods and aspect oriented models, plus the iterative and incremental Rational Unified Process.

topics.title: Agile Development
topics.definition: Agile development delivers working software in short iterations with continuous customer collaboration.

children.title: Agile manifesto and principles
children.definition: Individuals and interactions, working software, customer collaboration and response to change over processes, documentation, contracts and plans.

children.title: Extreme Programming (XP)
children.definition: Practices are planning games, small releases, simple design, test first development, pair programming and continuous integration.

children.title: Scrum
children.definition: Work is done in sprints of two to four weeks with a product backlog, sprint backlog, daily stand up, sprint review and retrospective.

children.title: Kanban and DevOps
children.definition: Kanban visualises work and limits work in progress; DevOps joins development and operations with continuous delivery.

children.title: Agile versus plan driven process
children.definition: Agile suits changing requirements and small co-located teams while plan driven suits stable requirements and contract heavy projects.

topics.title: Requirements Engineering
topics.definition: Requirements engineering establishes what the system must do, documented so that it can be validated and used for design.

children.title: Requirement types
children.definition: Functional requirements state services, non functional requirements state quality attributes, and domain requirements come from the application area.

children.title: Elicitation techniques
children.definition: Interviews, questionnaires, observation, document study, brainstorming, prototyping and joint application development.

children.title: Analysis and negotiation
children.definition: Classifying requirements, resolving conflicts between stakeholders and prioritising with techniques such as MoSCoW.

children.title: Specification and the SRS
children.definition: The Software Requirements Specification records functional and non-functional requirements, interfaces and constraints in structured or natural language form.

children.title: Validation and requirements review
children.definition: Checking completeness, consistency, feasibility and testability, including requirement traceability.

children.title: Requirements management and change
children.definition: Baselines, traceability matrices and a change control process keep requirements under control as the project evolves.

topics.title: Design Concepts
topics.definition: Design concepts are the principles that make a software design understandable, changeable and reliable.

children.title: Abstraction and refinement
children.definition: Abstraction hides detail at a given level while stepwise refinement adds detail gradually.

children.title: Modularity and information hiding
children.definition: Splitting a system into modules with hidden internals so a change stays local.

children.title: Coupling and cohesion
children.definition: Low coupling between modules and high cohesion inside a module give a maintainable design.

children.title: Refactoring and design classes
children.definition: Refactoring improves internal structure without changing behaviour; design classes add detail to analysis classes.

children.title: Design model elements
children.definition: Data design, architectural design, interface design and component level design together form the design model.

topics.title: Architectural Design
topics.definition: Architectural design defines the overall structure of the software in terms of components and their relationships.

children.title: Why architecture matters
children.definition: It supports communication, early design decisions, reuse and risk analysis.

children.title: Layered and client server styles
children.definition: Layered architecture stacks services; client server separates requesters from providers.

children.title: Model View Controller (MVC)
children.definition: Separates the model, the view and the controller so interface and logic can change independently.

children.title: Pipe and filter, repository, and call and return styles
children.definition: Pipes pass data through filters, repositories store shared data, and call and return structures use layers or main program with subprograms.

children.title: Service oriented and microservice architecture
children.definition: Independent services communicate over well defined interfaces, allowing separate deployment and scaling.

children.title: Architectural design decisions
children.definition: Choosing the style based on quality attributes such as performance, security, availability and maintainability.

topics.title: Component Level Design
topics.definition: Component level design describes each software component precisely enough to be implemented.

children.title: Component definition and types
children.definition: A component is a modular, deployable and replaceable part of a system with well defined interfaces.

children.title: Design principles and cohesion types
children.definition: Open-closed, dependency inversion and interface segregation principles, with cohesion from functional to coincidental.

children.title: Coupling types
children.definition: Content, common, control, stamp and data coupling, from bad to acceptable.

children.title: Class based and traditional components
children.definition: Object oriented design classes versus algorithmic modules, coupled with UML component and deployment diagrams.

children.title: Designing for reuse and testing
children.definition: Component interfaces should be simple and documented so other teams and tests can use them.

topics.title: User Interface Design
topics.definition: User interface design creates screens that allow users to work effectively with the system.

children.title: Golden rules of interface design
children.definition: Place the user in control, reduce the user memory load and make the interface consistent.

children.title: Usability and interface qualities
children.definition: Learnability, efficiency, error handling, memorability and satisfaction.

children.title: Interface design process
children.definition: Analyse users, tasks and environment; design the interface; prototype; evaluate with users and iterate.

children.title: Interface design issues
children.definition: Response time, help facilities, error messages, menu design, command labelling and accessibility.

children.title: Evaluation tools
children.definition: Heuristic evaluation, usability testing, questionnaires such as QUIS and think aloud protocols.

topics.title: Web Application Design
topics.definition: Web application design handles content, aesthetics, architecture, navigation and interface together.

children.title: Quality attributes of web apps
children.definition: Security, availability, scalability, maintainability, time to market and usability.

children.title: Aesthetic design
children.definition: Layout, colour, typography and graphics used to create a clear visual hierarchy.

children.title: Content design
children.definition: Organising and structuring text, images, audio and video, including content objects and their relationships.

children.title: Architecture and navigation design
children.definition: Choosing a web application architecture and designing navigation with menus, links, sitemaps and breadcrumbs.

children.title: Interface design for the web
children.definition: Consistent layout templates, responsive design, form design and clear error handling.

topics.title: Review Techniques
topics.definition: Reviews find defects early by having other people examine work products against criteria.

children.title: Informal reviews and desk checks
children.definition: Quick, low cost examination by peers or by the author before formal review.

children.title: Formal technical review (FTR)
children.definition: A structured meeting with roles of producer, reviewer, recorder and moderator, with a review checklist and recorded defects.

children.title: Walkthroughs and inspections
children.definition: A walkthrough is led by the author; an inspection is led by a trained moderator and is more rigorous and measured.

children.title: Review metrics and guidelines
children.definition: Defect density, preparation and rework time, review rate, and rules such as reviewing only a finished product and keeping tone constructive.

topics.title: Software Quality Assurance
topics.definition: SQA is the set of planned activities that give confidence that the product meets its quality requirements.

children.title: Quality concepts
children.definition: Quality of conformance, quality of design, fitness for purpose and the cost of quality.

children.title: SQA activities and tasks
children.definition: Standards, reviews, audits, testing strategy, defect tracking and measurement, with an SQA plan defining them.

children.title: Software standards
children.definition: ISO 9001 for quality management systems, ISO 25010 for product quality and IEEE standards for processes and documents.

children.title: Capability maturity models and Six Sigma
children.definition: CMMI maturity levels 1 to 5 and Six Sigma defect reduction, with DMAIC as its improvement cycle.

topics.title: Software Testing Strategies
topics.definition: A testing strategy organises test levels from individual units up to whole systems.

children.title: Verification and validation
children.definition: Verification asks whether the product is built right and validation whether the right product is built.

children.title: Unit testing and integration testing
children.definition: Units are tested in isolation; integration follows top down, bottom up, sandwich or big bang approaches.

children.title: Validation and system testing
children.definition: Tests against requirements, including alpha and beta testing with real users.

children.title: Regression and smoke testing
children.definition: Regression checks that changes broke nothing; smoke testing is a quick build verification.

children.title: White box and black box testing
children.definition: White box uses internal structure with basis path and condition testing; black box uses inputs and outputs with equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis.

children.title: Test documentation
children.definition: A test plan, test case specification, test procedure and defect report make testing reproducible.

topics.title: Software Configuration Management
topics.definition: Configuration management controls changes to all work products throughout the project life cycle.

children.title: Baselines and configuration items
children.definition: A baseline is a reviewed and approved state of a work product; configuration items are the products and documents under control.

children.title: Version control
children.definition: Repositories, check in and check out, branching and merging keep track of every change.

children.title: Change control
children.definition: A change request is evaluated for impact and cost, then approved or rejected by a change control board.

children.title: Release management and build
children.definition: Building, packaging and releasing consistent versions with release notes and rollback plans.

children.title: Desirable SCM features
children.definition: Identification, version control, change control, status accounting and audit, plus integration with the build.

topics.title: Product Metrics
topics.definition: Product metrics measure the quality and complexity of the software itself.

children.title: Measures, metrics and indicators
children.definition: A measure is a raw value, a metric relates measures and an indicator is a metric used for decision making.

children.title: Size oriented and function oriented metrics
children.definition: Lines of code and function points, where function points use inputs, outputs, enquiries, files and interfaces with complexity weights.

children.title: Complexity metrics
children.definition: Cyclomatic complexity counts decision points to show the required number of test paths; Halstead metrics use operators and operands.

children.title: Quality and reliability metrics
children.definition: Defect density, mean time between failures, usability and maintainability indices.

children.title: Object oriented metrics
children.definition: Weighted methods per class, depth of inheritance tree, coupling between objects and lack of cohesion.

topics.title: Project Management Concepts
topics.definition: Software project management plans, organises and controls the people, process and product so that the project meets its goals.

children.title: The four Ps
children.definition: People, product, process and project - the people factor is the most important.

children.title: Stakeholders and team structures
children.definition: Stakeholders include users, customers and management; teams may be closed, random, open or use the chief programmer model.

children.title: W5HH principle
children.definition: Why, what, when, who, where, how and how much give a complete project plan outline.

children.title: Common project risks and causes of failure
children.definition: Unrealistic deadlines, changing requirements, weak estimation and poor communication.

topics.title: Process and Project Metrics
topics.definition: Process metrics improve the development process while project metrics track a single project.

children.title: Measures, metrics and indicators
children.definition: Productivity, quality, effort and time measures turned into metrics and then indicators.

children.title: Software measurement and size
children.definition: Direct measures such as lines of code and cost, and indirect measures such as functionality, quality and complexity.

children.title: Reconciling process and product metrics
children.definition: Private individual data is aggregated into team and project metrics carefully to avoid misuse.

children.title: Metrics for software quality
children.definition: Correctness, maintainability, integrity and usability measured before delivery.

topics.title: Estimation for Software Projects
topics.definition: Estimation predicts the effort, cost and duration needed to build the software.

children.title: Estimation techniques
children.definition: Expert judgment, estimation by analogy, the Delphi method, Parkinson law and price to win.

children.title: Lines of code based estimation
children.definition: Estimate LOC and derive effort from historical productivity; depends heavily on the language used.

children.title: Function point based estimation
children.definition: Count unadjusted function points, adjust for complexity, then convert to lines of code using the language factor.

children.title: Use case point estimation
children.definition: Weight actors and use cases, adjust for technical and environmental factors, then convert to effort.

children.title: COCOMO model
children.definition: Organic, semi-detached and embedded modes estimate effort from size, with post-architecture multipliers for cost drivers.

children.title: Estimation accuracy
children.definition: Estimation is refined as the project proceeds, so ranges and confidence limits are used rather than a single number.

topics.title: Project Scheduling
topics.definition: Scheduling allocates work to people over time and shows how tasks depend on one another.

children.title: Work breakdown structure
children.definition: A hierarchical decomposition of the total work into tasks that can be estimated and assigned.

children.title: Task networks and dependencies
children.definition: Tasks are linked by finish to start, start to start and finish to finish relationships with lag where needed.

children.title: Gantt charts
children.definition: A calendar view of tasks and durations showing overlap and progress.

children.title: Critical path method and PERT
children.definition: Program evaluation and review technique uses optimistic, likely and pessimistic estimates to find the longest path, the critical path that fixes project duration.

children.title: Slack, float and tracking
children.definition: Slack is spare time in non-critical tasks; earned value analysis tracks schedule and cost performance.

children.title: Time boxing and agile scheduling
children.definition: Fixed short iterations with a flexible scope rather than a fixed scope with a flexible date.

topics.title: Risk Management
topics.definition: Risk management identifies what could go wrong and what will be done about it.

children.title: Risk concepts and types
children.definition: Project risks, technical risks, business risks and known or predictable unknown risks.

children.title: Risk identification and the risk table
children.definition: Brainstorming, checklists and past projects build a table listing risks, probability, impact and the risk factor.

children.title: Risk projection
children.definition: Assessing probability and impact, then computing the risk exposure.

children.title: Risk refinement and RMMM
children.definition: Risk mitigation, monitoring and management planning for each significant risk.

children.title: Risk and the software life cycle
children.definition: Risk exposure is highest early, so risky parts are prototyped or built first.

topics.title: Reliability Engineering
topics.definition: Reliability engineering measures and improves the probability that software runs without failure for a given time.

children.title: Reliability and availability defined
children.definition: Reliability is the probability of failure free operation; availability is the fraction of time the system is usable.

children.title: Reliability measures
children.definition: MTTF (mean time to failure), MTTR (mean time to repair), MTBF (mean time between failures) and availability = MTTF / (MTTF + MTTR).

children.title: Faults and failures
children.definition: A fault is a defect in the code, an error is an incorrect internal state and a failure is the observed wrong behaviour.

children.title: Hardware versus software reliability
children.definition: Hardware reliability falls with age due to wear, while software does not wear out but degrades as it is changed.

children.title: Reliability growth models
children.definition: Failure intensity decreases as defects are found and removed; models such as the basic execution time model predict this.

topics.title: Reliability Testing
topics.definition: Reliability testing measures failure intensity and tracks whether reliability is improving.

children.title: Failure intensity and reliability specification
children.definition: Failures per unit time or per transaction, tied to a target such as failures per thousand hours.

children.title: Software reliability metrics
children.definition: Probability of failure on demand, rate of occurrence of failures and mean time to failure.

children.title: Statistical testing and fault injection
children.definition: Tests are drawn from an operational profile which reflects real usage, and faults are injected to measure detection ability.

children.title: Reliability improvement cycles
children.definition: Track failure data, fix the worst faults, re-measure and continue until reliability targets are met.

topics.title: Security Requirements and Design
topics.definition: Secure engineering builds security in from requirements and design rather than adding it after coding.

children.title: Security requirement categories
children.definition: Confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication, authorisation, non-repudiation and auditing.

children.title: Security requirements elicitation
children.definition: Identify assets, threats, attackers and attack surfaces; misuse cases and threat modelling record what must be defended.

children.title: Threat modelling techniques
children.definition: STRIDE categories - spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service and elevation of privilege - with attack trees.

children.title: Secure design principles
children.definition: Least privilege, separation of duties, fail safe defaults, defence in depth, complete mediation and economy of mechanism.

children.title: Security patterns
children.definition: Reusable solutions such as authentication, authorisation, secure session and security logger patterns.

children.title: Security testing and review
children.definition: Static analysis, penetration testing, fuzzing, secure code review and vulnerability management after release.
